objective: reduce the dominant M89 finite-bank source cycles by an offline reversible within-row weight-bank permutation while preserving the exact parent, DAG, admission order and K6 fusion groups

bank_hashes.definition: feature position p inside each 256-bit source tile has weight_row=floor(p/8), base_bank=p mod 8; the tile offset is 32 rows and therefore does not change weight_row mod 8
bank_hashes.reversibility: for every weight row each hash is a permutation of banks 0..7, so bank depth and total weight bytes are unchanged
bank_hashes.selection: one fixed two-bit mode per operator chosen by aggregate source cycles across all ten samples; per-sample, per-group and runtime adaptation are forbidden

preservation_contract.runtime_logic: one three-bit XOR/add bank decoder, removable when modes are hardwired

required_outputs: per-operator and per-sample H0-H3 source cycles on unchanged union masks
sum over groups of ceil(union_popcount/8) tight mapping-independent lower bound
fixed per-operator winning modes and prohibited per-sample oracle upper bound
group, union-popcount, unique-issue and weight-byte conservation

stage2_integrated_replay.condition: run only if every stage1 gate passes
stage2_integrated_replay.requirement: replay the frozen group issue sequence with selected bank-skew durations through the existing M89 finite context, parent, response and accumulator calendars

kill_conditions: H0 fails exact M89 reproduction or any group/union/work/byte identity changes
stage1 source improvement is below 0.5 percent or any sample regresses
a winning mode requires per-sample, per-group or runtime adaptation
stage2 integrated, p95, dependency or occupancy gate fails
the implementation requires an extra SRAM port, extra weight row, replicated weight vector or cross-group scheduler change

claim_policy.stage2_admitted_after_validation: frozen-cohort module transaction-model cycle comparison only
forbidden: RTL correctness, SRAM macro feasibility, synthesized PPA or energy
accuracy, equal-area, full-network, system, DATE headline or best-paper claim
